newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-GIOVANNI, RONALDO SCORE TWO EACH IN BRAZIL WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GIOVANNI, RONALDO SCORE TWO EACH IN BRAZIL WIN.

text.p: Giovanni and Ronaldo scored two goals each as Brazil beat Poland 4-2 in their first soccer international of the year on Wednesday.

Striker Romario, making his first national team appearance since the 1994 World Cup final, failed to get on the scoresheet and missed an open net. But his much-vaunted partnership with Ronaldo in attack was responsible for two of the Brazil goals.

The first came in the 48th minute when Brazil won a free kick near the Poland penalty area. Romario quickly slipped the ball to Ronaldo, who turned and scored with a left-foot shot as a dozy Polish defence helplessly looked on.
In the 72nd minute, Romario outwitted a Polish defender and flicked the ball to Ronaldo, who blasted a right-foot shot into the net.
Giovanni, Ronaldo's teammate at Spanish club Barcelona, had set up the win with two first-half goals.
Poland scored twice in the last four minutes on goals by substitute Cezary Kucharski and Marek Citko, who scored from a rebound after seeing his penalty saved by Carlos Germano.

Romario had been left in the cold by coach Mario Zagallo after snubbing a call-up two years ago. But Zagallo relented last week after claiming that Romario's behaviour, which has often been his undoing, had improved.
"Unfortunately, I didn't score but I'm happy with my performance," Romario said. "I've always said that if I got another chance, I intended to stay (with the team). It depends on God and me."
Poland, like many other middle-ranking European sides, played some neat midfield but were ultimately short of creative ideas in attack until their late revival made the score respectable.

The Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) opted for a local referee and Antonio Perreira da Silva clearly had diplomacy on his mind as he overlooked several crude Polish tackles early on. The Polish defence also got the benefit of the doubt on at least two close-cut offside decisions.
Brazil suffered an early fright when Poland striker Krzysztof Warzycha fired narrowly wide from inside the penalty area in the second minute.
But five minutes later Giovanni opened the scoring, calmly placing the ball under the body of goalkeeper Grzegorz Szamotulski.

Giovanni scored again on Brazil's next real chance 19 minutes later. This time, Romario split the Polish defence, Leonardo latched onto the ball, rounded Szamotulski and laid on a pass for Giovanni to place into the empty net.
Poland had enjoyed plenty of possession until that point but in the second half they tired and Brazil began to turn on the style the public had expected.

Romario missed his chance for glory with the score at 3-0 when, with the goal at his mercy, he stubbed the ball wide from six metres. However, he still produced a couple of moments of skill that sent the crowd into delirium.
